title: Deep Learning Indaba artificial intelligence challenges / Portefeuille IAPD-FCDO : Deep Learning Indaba AI Challenges (défis d'IA de la conférence Deep Learning Indaba)
description: The Artificial Intelligence for Development (AI4D) program is a partnership between IDRC and the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). The partnership aims to create an inclusive and responsible artificial intelligence (AI) ecosystem through the scaling of AI innovations and policies that improve the quality of life for all in Africa and beyond. Effective capacity strengthening and knowledge sharing, which enhances the visibility, relevance and influence of the solutions AI4D will support, are critical to achieving this vision.   This project aims to strengthen the African machine learning and artificial intelligence community by supporting the Deep Learning Indaba (DLI) conference. The mission of DLI, an annual meeting of the African machine learning and AI community, is to ensure that Africans are not just observers and receivers of the ongoing advances in AI but are also active shapers and owners of these technological advances. This grassroots, African-led conference aims to address the significant gap between the technological advancements occurring globally and the local capacity and expertise to adapt and innovate using responsible AI technologies across Africa. This represents a significant expansion of the reach of the AI4D network and will enable progress to be made in promoting responsible AI innovation that addresses local and global challenges. It will make AI education and research accessible across the continent to the thousands of Africans and dozens of communities and local chapters that make up the Indaba community. AI4D will support DLI with scholarships to ensure attendees, in particular women and people with disabilities, have access to the event without financial barriers. It will also support an Ideathon program to generate solutions to annually set development challenges in the region and provide the winning ideas with mentorship and a financial award. title: Laying the foundations for artificial intelligence for development (AI4D) in Africa
description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) may sound futuristic, but it has profound implications for human development across Africa right now. A burgeoning community of AI practitioners and researchers across the continent are working to apply their machine-learning skills to tackle local challenges in new ways. However, many barriers prevent the use of AI in ways that support human rights and inclusive benefits. These barriers include governments with limited capacity to integrate AI into their operations and service delivery, gender disparities within the community of practice, and limited resources to enable machine-learning practitioners to exchange and learn amongst each other.   The goal of this project is to support the development of a vibrant AI for development ecosystem in Africa that lays the foundation for the rights-based and inclusive implementation of AI for the public good. This project will build on past IDRC support for the development of a pan-African machine-learning community of practice to provide continuity and support for key regional events that galvanize the community. The project will also support a second round of the Government AI Readiness Index, which seeks to capture the capacity of governments to successfully exploit AIs to improve operations and service delivery.

title: Digital new deal for Africa
description: Networking technologies are now firmly embedded in the core of many economic, social, and political activities around the world. However, the benefits of the digitization of the economy and society remain extremely uneven between countries and within them. Benefits have also been accompanied by collective and individual risks. For example, otherwise beneficial networking tools (mostly mobile devices) are also being used for surveillance, tracking, censorship, and repression all around the world. In addition, global digital platforms are extracting economic value from personal data, further amplified through algorithms, which in turn help them grow into globally influential corporations with immense power over people's data and decisions. The shift in traditional power relations between states, markets, and citizens in global governance has blurred notions of what constitutes public and private, national and international, and has left a governance vacuum. After decades of private interests dominating data governance, public regulation of the internet has gained international attention to try to regulate global platforms that are commodifying data with little regard for the implications on democratic governance and human rights.  This project is part of an overall process to strengthen cyber policy centres in the Global South. It aims to ensure that policymakers in Africa are using objective, high-quality research to inform digital policy development. It will contribute to building the institutional capacity and sustainability of Research ICT Africa to produce credible, legitimate, and locally relevant research that brings together different perspectives on critical policy issues such as artificial intelligence, data, and internet governance challenges. title: Harnessing the Economic Power of Data in the Middle East and North Africa
description: This project will explore the potential of innovative technologies and approaches to improve data collection, management, and usability with the goal of enhancing entrepreneurship and youth employment in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA). Technology leading changeNew technologies and applications, such as mobile phones and social media, are leading to an exponential increase in the volume and types of data available. This creates unprecedented possibilities for informing and transforming society. A number of innovative initiatives using mobile technology, crowd-sourcing, and other tools currently gather vital data to track and monitor outcomes in real time. A recent study in Indonesia found that public tweets mentioning food prices closely reflect actual food prices. This has led to the development of a tool that extracts daily food prices from public tweets to produce a real-time food price index. This data mining approach could be adapted to other development issues and locations, leveraging Twitter and other social media.Data to boost youth entrepreneurshipThe need for more and better data is particularly important in MENA. The region faces a wide range of development challenges. One of the most pressing is youth unemployment with a rate of 26-29%. Better quality data, and more relevant data could provide the region with valuable information that would lead to more effective policies to promote youth employment. It could also become a valuable business resource for data-entrepreneurs, notably MENA's youth.Project objectivesThe American University in Cairo will lead the project, working in partnership with Birzeit University and Al Akhawayn University. The project has the following specific objectives:-inform policies and regulations to effectively produce, manage, and use data, particularly for entrepreneurship and youth employment-study, develop, and test innovative approaches to produce, manage, and use data-build capacities in data production, management, and use among policymakers, statistical agencies, NGOs, and youth-disseminate knowledge and lessons learned from the project -engage key stakeholders, including NGOs, entrepreneurs, journalists, researchers, and the public
